# Attributes offered for each dataset in R's datasets package. Only attributes that can be averaged
# are listed: factors, category codes (mtcars$vs, mtcars$am), and indices (airquality$Month,
# airquality$Day, morley$Expt, morley$Run, ChickWeight$Time) are deliberately absent. A dataset that
# is a single series (time series, named vector, the volcano matrix) contributes one attribute, named
# after what its values measure.
raw_attributes_by_dataset <- list(
  AirPassengers = list(passengers = datasets::AirPassengers),
  airquality = datasets::airquality[c("Ozone", "Solar.R", "Wind", "Temp")],
  cars = datasets::cars[c("speed", "dist")],
  ChickWeight = list(weight = datasets::ChickWeight$weight),
  discoveries = list(discoveries = datasets::discoveries),
  faithful = datasets::faithful[c("eruptions", "waiting")],
  InsectSprays = datasets::InsectSprays["count"],
  iris = datasets::iris[c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width", "Petal.Length", "Petal.Width")],
  islands = list(area = datasets::islands),
  lynx = list(trappings = datasets::lynx),
  morley = datasets::morley["Speed"],
  mtcars = datasets::mtcars[c("mpg", "cyl", "disp", "hp", "drat", "wt", "qsec", "gear", "carb")],
  Nile = list(flow = datasets::Nile),
  precip = list(precipitation = datasets::precip),
  pressure = datasets::pressure[c("temperature", "pressure")],
  quakes = datasets::quakes[c("lat", "long", "depth", "mag", "stations")],
  rivers = list(length = datasets::rivers),
  sunspot.year = list(sunspots = datasets::sunspot.year),
  swiss = datasets::swiss[c("Fertility", "Agriculture", "Examination", "Education", "Catholic", "Infant.Mortality")],
  trees = datasets::trees[c("Girth", "Height", "Volume")],
  USArrests = datasets::USArrests[c("Murder", "Assault", "UrbanPop", "Rape")],
  volcano = list(height = datasets::volcano),
  warpbreaks = datasets::warpbreaks["breaks"],
  women = datasets::women[c("height", "weight")]
)

greatest_common_divisor <- function(first_integer, second_integer) {
  while (second_integer > 0) {
    remainder <- first_integer %% second_integer
    first_integer <- second_integer
    second_integer <- remainder
  }
  first_integer
}

# When every value equals minimum + k * unit for an integer k, the mean of n values equals
# minimum + j * (unit / n) for an integer j. Histogram bins aligned to that grid hold equal numbers of
# attainable means, which keeps discrete attributes from drawing comb-shaped histograms.
# Returns 0 when no unit with at most six decimal places fits every value (treated as continuous).
lattice_unit_of <- function(values) {
  offsets <- values - min(values)
  for (decimal_places in 0:6) {
    scaled_offsets <- offsets * 10^decimal_places
    # Above 2^52 a double has no fractional part left to test, so no lattice can be detected.
    if (max(scaled_offsets) > 2^52) {
      break
    }
    integer_offsets <- round(x = scaled_offsets)
    if (all(abs(x = scaled_offsets - integer_offsets) < 1e-6) && any(integer_offsets > 0)) {
      return(Reduce(f = greatest_common_divisor, x = integer_offsets[integer_offsets > 0]) / 10^decimal_places)
    }
  }
  0
}

# Mean and standard deviation with divisor N (the values are the entire population being sampled),
# computed on values scaled by their largest magnitude so that neither can overflow.
population_moments <- function(values) {
  largest_magnitude <- max(abs(x = values))
  if (largest_magnitude == 0) {
    return(list(mean = 0, standard_deviation = 0))
  }
  scaled_values <- values / largest_magnitude
  scaled_mean <- mean(x = scaled_values)
  list(
    mean = largest_magnitude * scaled_mean,
    standard_deviation = largest_magnitude * sqrt(x = mean(x = (scaled_values - scaled_mean)^2))
  )
}

# Describes why values cannot form a population, or returns NULL when they can. A population needs at
# least two values, all finite, small enough that a sum of 100 of them stays finite, and a spread
# large enough to draw, both in absolute terms and relative to the values' size (double precision
# carries about 16 significant digits).
population_problem <- function(values) {
  if (length(x = values) < 2L) {
    return("has fewer than two values")
  }
  if (!all(is.finite(x = values))) {
    return("has values that are not finite")
  }
  if (max(abs(x = values)) > 1e300) {
    return("has values too large to average")
  }
  standard_deviation <- population_moments(values = values)$standard_deviation
  if (standard_deviation == 0) {
    return("has the same value everywhere, so its sample means cannot vary")
  }
  if (standard_deviation < 1e-290) {
    return("varies too little to draw")
  }
  if (standard_deviation < 1e-7 * max(abs(x = values))) {
    return("varies too little relative to its size to draw precisely")
  }
  NULL
}

# The only constructor for a population, so every population satisfies the invariants above.
make_population <- function(dataset_name, attribute_name, values) {
  problem <- population_problem(values = values)
  if (!is.null(problem)) {
    stop(errorCondition(message = paste0(dataset_name, "$", attribute_name, " ", problem, "."), call = NULL))
  }
  moments <- population_moments(values = values)
  list(
    dataset_name = dataset_name,
    attribute_name = attribute_name,
    values = values,
    mean = moments$mean,
    standard_deviation = moments$standard_deviation,
    lattice_unit = lattice_unit_of(values = values)
  )
}

population_key <- function(dataset_name, attribute_name) {
  paste0(dataset_name, "$", attribute_name)
}

population_catalog <- list()
for (dataset_name in names(x = raw_attributes_by_dataset)) {
  for (attribute_name in names(x = raw_attributes_by_dataset[[dataset_name]])) {
    attribute_values <- as.numeric(x = raw_attributes_by_dataset[[dataset_name]][[attribute_name]])
    population_catalog[[population_key(dataset_name = dataset_name, attribute_name = attribute_name)]] <- make_population(
      dataset_name = dataset_name,
      attribute_name = attribute_name,
      # Missing values (airquality has them) are not part of the population.
      values = attribute_values[!is.na(x = attribute_values)]
    )
  }
}

dataset_names <- names(x = raw_attributes_by_dataset)
dataset_names <- dataset_names[order(tolower(x = dataset_names), method = "radix")]

# Attribute dropdown choices per dataset: each label is an attribute name and each value is the key of
# that attribute's population, so a selected attribute always identifies exactly one population.
attribute_choices_by_dataset <- lapply(
  X = stats::setNames(object = dataset_names, nm = dataset_names),
  FUN = function(dataset_name) {
    attribute_names <- names(x = raw_attributes_by_dataset[[dataset_name]])
    stats::setNames(
      object = population_key(dataset_name = dataset_name, attribute_name = attribute_names),
      nm = attribute_names
    )
  }
)

```{r transform, include = FALSE}
# Names a transform formula may use besides x. Any other name is rejected before evaluation, and
# evaluation happens in an environment holding only these names, so a formula can compute but cannot
# act: no assignment, no files, no system calls, no access to other objects.
formula_base_names <- c(
  "(", "+", "-", "*", "/", "^", "%%", "%/%",
  "<", ">", "<=", ">=", "==", "!=", "&", "|", "!", "ifelse",
  "abs", "sign", "sqrt", "exp", "expm1", "log", "log10", "log2", "log1p",
  "sin", "cos", "tan", "asin", "acos", "atan", "atan2", "sinpi", "cospi", "tanpi",
  "sinh", "cosh", "tanh", "asinh", "acosh", "atanh",
  "floor", "ceiling", "round", "signif", "trunc",
  "gamma", "lgamma", "beta", "lbeta", "choose", "lchoose", "factorial", "lfactorial",
  "pmin", "pmax", "min", "max", "sum", "mean", "length", "rank"
)
formula_stats_names <- c("median", "sd", "var", "pnorm", "qnorm", "plogis", "qlogis")
formula_bindings <- c(
  mget(x = formula_base_names, envir = baseenv()),
  mget(x = formula_stats_names, envir = asNamespace(ns = "stats")),
  list(pi = pi, T = TRUE, F = FALSE)
)

formula_problem <- function(message) {
  stop(errorCondition(message = message, class = "formula_problem", call = NULL))
}

# Applies y = f(x) to every value x of a population. Returns the transformed population, or signals a
# formula_problem condition whose message says what to fix.
transform_population <- function(population, formula_text) {
  if (!is.character(x = formula_text) || length(x = formula_text) != 1L || !nzchar(x = trimws(x = formula_text))) {
    formula_problem(message = "Type a formula in x, such as log(x + 1).")
  }
  parsed <- tryCatch(expr = parse(text = formula_text, keep.source = FALSE), error = function(condition) NULL)
  if (is.null(parsed)) {
    formula_problem(message = "The formula is not valid R code.")
  }
  if (length(x = parsed) != 1L) {
    formula_problem(message = "The formula must be a single expression in x.")
  }
  formula_expression <- parsed[[1L]]
  # "y ~ log(x)" and "~ log(x)" are read the same as "log(x)".
  if (is.call(x = formula_expression) && identical(x = formula_expression[[1L]], y = as.name(x = "~"))) {
    if (length(x = formula_expression) == 2L) {
      formula_expression <- formula_expression[[2L]]
    } else if (identical(x = formula_expression[[2L]], y = as.name(x = "y"))) {
      formula_expression <- formula_expression[[3L]]
    } else {
      formula_problem(message = "The left side of the formula must be y.")
    }
  }
  used_names <- all.names(expr = formula_expression, unique = TRUE)
  unavailable_names <- setdiff(x = used_names, y = c("x", names(x = formula_bindings)))
  if (length(x = unavailable_names) > 0L) {
    formula_problem(message = paste0(
      "`", unavailable_names[[1L]], "`",
      " is not available in formulas. Use x, numbers, pi, arithmetic, and functions such as log, exp, sqrt, and abs."
    ))
  }
  if (!("x" %in% used_names)) {
    formula_problem(message = "The formula must use x.")
  }

  sandbox <- list2env(x = c(formula_bindings, list(x = population$values)), parent = emptyenv())
  result <- tryCatch(
    expr = withCallingHandlers(
      expr = eval(expr = formula_expression, envir = sandbox),
      # Warnings such as "NaNs produced" are superseded by the finiteness check below.
      warning = function(condition) invokeRestart(r = "muffleWarning")
    ),
    error = function(condition) {
      formula_problem(message = paste0("R could not evaluate the formula: ", conditionMessage(c = condition)))
    }
  )
  if (!(is.numeric(x = result) || is.logical(x = result))) {
    formula_problem(message = "The formula must produce numbers.")
  }
  if (length(x = result) != length(x = population$values)) {
    formula_problem(message = "The formula must produce one value for each value of x.")
  }
  transformed_values <- as.numeric(x = result)
  undefined <- !is.finite(x = transformed_values)
  if (any(undefined)) {
    formula_problem(message = sprintf(
      fmt = "The formula is undefined or infinite for %d of %d values of x, for example x = %s.",
      sum(undefined),
      length(x = undefined),
      format(x = population$values[which(x = undefined)[[1L]]], digits = 6)
    ))
  }
  problem <- population_problem(values = transformed_values)
  if (!is.null(problem)) {
    formula_problem(message = paste0("The transformed attribute ", problem, "."))
  }
  # The transformed attribute is named by the formula with x replaced by the attribute's name.
  named_expression <- do.call(
    what = substitute,
    args = list(expr = formula_expression, env = list(x = as.name(x = population$attribute_name)))
  )
  make_population(
    dataset_name = population$dataset_name,
    attribute_name = paste(deparse(expr = named_expression, width.cutoff = 500L), collapse = " "),
    values = transformed_values
  )
}
```

```{r sampling, include = FALSE}
# Every sample draws sample_size values independently and with replacement, so each sample mean has
# expectation mu and standard deviation sigma / sqrt(n) exactly.
simulate_sample_means <- function(population, sample_size, number_of_samples) {
  draw_indices <- sample.int(n = length(x = population$values), size = sample_size * number_of_samples, replace = TRUE)
  samples <- matrix(data = population$values[draw_indices], nrow = number_of_samples, ncol = sample_size)
  list(
    population = population,
    sample_size = sample_size,
    number_of_samples = number_of_samples,
    sample_means = rowMeans(x = samples),
    most_recent_sample = samples[number_of_samples, ],
    standard_error = population$standard_deviation / sqrt(x = sample_size)
  )
}

# Histogram bins for the sample means. The target width is Scott's normal reference rule evaluated at
# the known standard deviation of the sample mean, narrowed when needed so that a small number of
# samples still spreads over at least five bins. On a lattice, the width becomes a whole number of
# lattice steps and every edge sits halfway between attainable means; otherwise a bin is centered on mu.
sample_mean_bins <- function(simulation) {
  minimum_number_of_bins <- 5
  maximum_number_of_bins <- 200
  population <- simulation$population
  sample_means <- simulation$sample_means
  span_of_means <- max(sample_means) - min(sample_means)
  target_width <- 3.49 * simulation$standard_error * simulation$number_of_samples^(-1 / 3)
  if (span_of_means > 0) {
    target_width <- min(target_width, span_of_means / minimum_number_of_bins)
  }
  lattice_spacing <- population$lattice_unit / simulation$sample_size
  if (lattice_spacing > 0) {
    steps_per_bin <- max(
      1,
      round(x = target_width / lattice_spacing),
      ceiling(x = span_of_means / (maximum_number_of_bins * lattice_spacing))
    )
    bin_width <- steps_per_bin * lattice_spacing
    lattice_origin <- min(population$values)
    step_nearest_mean <- round(x = (population$mean - lattice_origin) / lattice_spacing)
    reference_edge <- lattice_origin + (step_nearest_mean - floor(x = (steps_per_bin - 1) / 2) - 0.5) * lattice_spacing
  } else {
    bin_width <- max(target_width, span_of_means / maximum_number_of_bins)
    reference_edge <- population$mean - bin_width / 2
  }
  first_edge <- reference_edge + bin_width * floor(x = (min(sample_means) - reference_edge) / bin_width)
  number_of_bins <- max(1, ceiling(x = (max(sample_means) - first_edge) / bin_width))
  edges <- first_edge + bin_width * (0:number_of_bins)
  bin_of_each_mean <- findInterval(x = sample_means, vec = edges, all.inside = TRUE)
  counts <- tabulate(bin = bin_of_each_mean, nbins = number_of_bins)
  list(
    edges = edges,
    bin_width = bin_width,
    densities = counts / (length(x = sample_means) * bin_width)
  )
}
```

```{r drawing, include = FALSE}
# Plots are drawn on a transparent background over the white slide; "surface" is the slide color, used
# for the gaps between bars and the rings around points.
widget_colors <- list(
  surface = "#ffffff",
  primary_ink = "#0b0b0b",
  secondary_ink = "#52514e",
  baseline = "#c3c2b7",
  sample_fill = "#cfcdc6",
  sample_point = "#6f6d67",
  population_mean = "#e34948",
  standard_deviation = "#2a78d6"
)

as_plot_label <- function(label) {
  if (nzchar(x = label)) latex2exp::TeX(input = label) else ""
}

# Labels for the lines at mu + k * sigma / sqrt(n), from most to least descriptive. Each plot uses the
# first set whose widest label fits in 80 percent of the gap between neighboring lines, so labels never
# overlap; the last set labels mu alone.
standard_deviation_label_sets <- lapply(
  X = list(
    c(r"($\mu - 2\sigma/\sqrt{n}$)", r"($\mu - \sigma/\sqrt{n}$)", r"($\mu$)", r"($\mu + \sigma/\sqrt{n}$)", r"($\mu + 2\sigma/\sqrt{n}$)"),
    c(r"($-2\sigma/\sqrt{n}$)", r"($-\sigma/\sqrt{n}$)", r"($\mu$)", r"($+\sigma/\sqrt{n}$)", r"($+2\sigma/\sqrt{n}$)"),
    c(r"($-2$)", r"($-1$)", r"($\mu$)", r"($+1$)", r"($+2$)"),
    c("", "", r"($\mu$)", "", "")
  ),
  FUN = function(labels) lapply(X = labels, FUN = as_plot_label)
)

# Plain numbers for ordinary magnitudes; scientific notation, with enough digits to tell neighboring
# ticks apart, for the very large or very small magnitudes a transform can produce.
format_tick_labels <- function(ticks) {
  nonzero_magnitudes <- abs(x = ticks[ticks != 0])
  if (length(x = nonzero_magnitudes) == 0L || (max(nonzero_magnitudes) < 1e15 && min(nonzero_magnitudes) >= 1e-6)) {
    return(format(x = ticks, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE))
  }
  tick_step <- if (length(x = ticks) > 1L) min(diff(x = sort(x = ticks))) else max(nonzero_magnitudes)
  significant_digits <- min(15, max(1, ceiling(x = log10(x = max(nonzero_magnitudes) / tick_step)) + 1))
  format(x = ticks, scientific = TRUE, digits = significant_digits, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)
}

# A zero-width range (for example, a sample whose values are all equal) is widened so it can be drawn.
widen_degenerate_limits <- function(limits) {
  if (diff(x = limits) > 0) {
    return(limits)
  }
  limits + c(-1, 1) * max(0.1 * abs(x = limits[1]), 0.5)
}

# Opens a plot whose left margin fits the widest horizontal y tick label and whose right margin fits
# the rightmost x tick label, then draws both axes and their titles. y_axis_style "i" starts the bars
# exactly at the baseline; "r" pads the range by 4 percent. The x range is always padded by 4 percent.
open_plot <- function(x_limits, y_limits, y_axis_style, x_title, y_title, top_margin_lines) {
  x_limits <- widen_degenerate_limits(limits = x_limits)
  y_limits <- widen_degenerate_limits(limits = y_limits)
  axis_cex <- 0.85
  inches_per_margin_line <- graphics::par("csi") * graphics::par("mex")
  label_lines <- function(labels) graphics::strwidth(s = labels, units = "inches", cex = axis_cex) / inches_per_margin_line

  y_padding <- if (identical(x = y_axis_style, y = "r")) 0.04 * diff(x = y_limits) else 0
  y_ticks <- grDevices::axisTicks(usr = y_limits + c(-1, 1) * y_padding, log = FALSE)
  y_tick_labels <- format_tick_labels(ticks = y_ticks)
  y_title_line <- 0.55 + max(label_lines(labels = y_tick_labels)) + 0.6
  left_margin_lines <- y_title_line + 1.2

  x_axis_range <- x_limits + c(-1, 1) * 0.04 * diff(x = x_limits)
  x_ticks <- grDevices::axisTicks(usr = x_axis_range, log = FALSE)
  x_tick_labels <- format_tick_labels(ticks = x_ticks)
  plot_width_lines <- graphics::par("fin")[1] / inches_per_margin_line - left_margin_lines - 0.8
  last_tick_to_edge_lines <- (x_axis_range[2] - max(x_ticks)) / diff(x = x_axis_range) * plot_width_lines
  right_margin_lines <- max(0.8, label_lines(labels = x_tick_labels[length(x = x_tick_labels)]) / 2 - last_tick_to_edge_lines + 0.3)

  graphics::par(
    mar = c(3.4, left_margin_lines, top_margin_lines, right_margin_lines),
    mgp = c(2.2, 0.55, 0),
    las = 1,
    tcl = -0.3,
    bg = "transparent"
  )
  graphics::plot.new()
  graphics::plot.window(xlim = x_limits, ylim = y_limits, yaxs = y_axis_style)
  axis_style <- list(
    col = widget_colors$baseline,
    col.ticks = widget_colors$baseline,
    col.axis = widget_colors$secondary_ink,
    lwd = 1,
    cex.axis = axis_cex
  )
  do.call(what = graphics::axis, args = c(list(side = 1, at = x_ticks, labels = x_tick_labels), axis_style))
  do.call(what = graphics::axis, args = c(list(side = 2, at = y_ticks, labels = y_tick_labels), axis_style))
  graphics::title(xlab = x_title, col.lab = widget_colors$secondary_ink, cex.lab = 0.95)
  graphics::title(ylab = y_title, line = y_title_line, col.lab = widget_colors$secondary_ink, cex.lab = 0.95)
}

draw_sampling_distribution <- function(simulation) {
  population <- simulation$population
  standard_error <- simulation$standard_error
  bins <- sample_mean_bins(simulation = simulation)
  number_of_bins <- length(x = bins$densities)
  x_limits <- range(bins$edges, population$mean + c(-3.5, 3.5) * standard_error)
  curve_x <- seq(from = x_limits[1], to = x_limits[2], length.out = 501L)
  curve_density <- stats::dnorm(x = curve_x, mean = population$mean, sd = standard_error)
  y_limits <- c(0, 1.06 * max(bins$densities, curve_density))
  line_offsets <- -2:2
  line_positions <- population$mean + line_offsets * standard_error
  label_cex <- 0.85

  open_plot(
    x_limits = x_limits,
    y_limits = y_limits,
    y_axis_style = "i",
    x_title = population$attribute_name,
    y_title = "Density",
    top_margin_lines = 1.6
  )

  # A surface-colored gap separates adjacent bars when the bars are wide enough to keep it.
  pixels_per_unit <- abs(x = diff(x = graphics::grconvertX(x = x_limits, from = "user", to = "device"))) / diff(x = x_limits)
  bar_pixels <- bins$bin_width * pixels_per_unit
  graphics::rect(
    xleft = bins$edges[-(number_of_bins + 1L)],
    ybottom = 0,
    xright = bins$edges[-1L],
    ytop = bins$densities,
    col = widget_colors$sample_fill,
    border = if (bar_pixels >= 6) widget_colors$surface else NA,
    lwd = if (bar_pixels >= 10) 2 else 1
  )
  graphics::segments(
    x0 = line_positions[line_offsets != 0],
    y0 = 0,
    x1 = line_positions[line_offsets != 0],
    y1 = y_limits[2],
    col = widget_colors$standard_deviation,
    lwd = 1.5
  )
  graphics::segments(
    x0 = population$mean,
    y0 = 0,
    x1 = population$mean,
    y1 = y_limits[2],
    col = widget_colors$population_mean,
    lwd = 2,
    lty = "dashed"
  )
  graphics::lines(x = curve_x, y = curve_density, col = widget_colors$primary_ink, lwd = 2)
  graphics::abline(h = 0, col = widget_colors$baseline, lwd = 1)

  label_width <- function(label) graphics::strwidth(s = label, units = "user", cex = label_cex)
  chosen_labels <- standard_deviation_label_sets[[length(x = standard_deviation_label_sets)]]
  for (label_set in standard_deviation_label_sets) {
    if (max(vapply(X = label_set, FUN = label_width, FUN.VALUE = numeric(length = 1L))) <= 0.8 * standard_error) {
      chosen_labels <- label_set
      break
    }
  }
  for (index in seq_along(along.with = line_positions)) {
    graphics::mtext(
      text = chosen_labels[[index]],
      side = 3,
      at = line_positions[index],
      line = 0.3,
      cex = label_cex,
      col = widget_colors$secondary_ink
    )
  }
}

draw_most_recent_sample <- function(simulation) {
  sample_values <- simulation$most_recent_sample
  quantile_pairs <- stats::qqnorm(y = sample_values, plot.it = FALSE)

  open_plot(
    x_limits = range(quantile_pairs$x),
    y_limits = range(quantile_pairs$y),
    y_axis_style = "r",
    x_title = "Theoretical Quantiles",
    y_title = "Sample Quantiles",
    top_margin_lines = 0.8
  )
  # Reference line through the first and third quartiles, as in stats::qqline.
  stats::qqline(y = sample_values, col = widget_colors$primary_ink, lwd = 2)
  graphics::points(
    x = quantile_pairs$x,
    y = quantile_pairs$y,
    pch = 21,
    bg = widget_colors$sample_point,
    col = widget_colors$surface,
    lwd = 1,
    cex = 1.1
  )
}
```

```{r widget_definition, include = FALSE}
widget_interface <- shiny::fluidPage(
  shiny::tags$head(
    shiny::tags$link(rel = "stylesheet", href = "https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Open+Sans:wght@400;600&display=swap"),
    shiny::tags$style(shiny::HTML(text = "
      html, body { background: transparent; }
      body { font-family: 'Open Sans', Arial, sans-serif; color: #0b0b0b; }
      .control-label { font-weight: 600; }
      .form-group { margin-bottom: 6px; }
      .checkbox { margin-top: 4px; margin-bottom: 4px; }
      .formula-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin: 2px 0 0 20px; }
      .formula-row > label { margin: 0; font-weight: 400; white-space: nowrap; }
      .formula-row > .form-group { flex: 1 1 auto; margin: 0; }
      .formula-row input { height: 30px; padding: 4px 8px; font-family: Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; }
      .formula-row.is-disabled > label, .formula-row.is-disabled input { color: #b0afa9; }
      .display-area { display: flex; gap: 24px; align-items: flex-start; border-top: 1px solid #e1e0d9; margin-top: 4px; padding-top: 4px; }
      .display-area > .main-panel { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; }
      .display-area > .side-panel { flex: 0 0 300px; }
      .display-area h3 { font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; margin: 4px 0 2px 0; }
      .display-area h4 { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; margin: 8px 0 4px 0; }
    ")),
    # The formula row is greyed out and locked whenever Apply Transform is unchecked. The formula box
    # holds code, so the browser neither spell-checks nor autocompletes it.
    shiny::tags$script(shiny::HTML(text = "
      $(function() {
        function synchronizeFormulaRow() {
          var transformApplied = $('#apply_transform').prop('checked');
          $('#transform_formula').prop('disabled', !transformApplied);
          $('.formula-row').toggleClass('is-disabled', !transformApplied);
        }
        $('#transform_formula').attr({ autocomplete: 'off', spellcheck: 'false' });
        $(document).on('change', '#apply_transform', synchronizeFormulaRow);
        synchronizeFormulaRow();
      });
    "))
  ),
  # Native dropdowns (selectize = FALSE) always hold a selection, so neither can be emptied.
  shiny::fluidRow(
    shiny::column(
      width = 3,
      shiny::selectInput(
        inputId = "dataset",
        label = "Dataset",
        choices = dataset_names,
        selected = dataset_names[[1L]],
        selectize = FALSE,
        width = "100%"
      )
    ),
    shiny::column(
      width = 3,
      shiny::selectInput(
        inputId = "attribute",
        label = "Attribute",
        choices = attribute_choices_by_dataset[[dataset_names[[1L]]]],
        selectize = FALSE,
        width = "100%"
      )
    ),
    shiny::column(
      width = 6,
      shiny::sliderInput(inputId = "sample_size", label = "Sample Size", min = 1, max = 100, value = 10, step = 1, ticks = FALSE, width = "100%"),
      shiny::sliderInput(inputId = "number_of_samples", label = "Number of Samples", min = 10, max = 10000, value = 1000, step = 10, ticks = FALSE, width = "100%"),
      shiny::checkboxInput(inputId = "show_quantile_quantile", label = "QQ", value = FALSE),
      shiny::checkboxInput(inputId = "apply_transform", label = "Apply Transform", value = FALSE),
      shiny::div(
        class = "formula-row is-disabled",
        shiny::tags$label(`for` = "transform_formula", "Formula: y~"),
        shiny::textInput(inputId = "transform_formula", label = NULL, value = "log(x)", width = "100%")
      )
    )
  ),
  # The quantile-quantile panel takes a fixed width beside the main panel while its checkbox is checked;
  # otherwise the main panel spans the whole display area.
  shiny::div(
    class = "display-area",
    shiny::div(
      class = "main-panel",
      shiny::tags$h3("Distribution of Sample Means"),
      shiny::plotOutput(outputId = "sampling_distribution", height = "340px")
    ),
    shiny::conditionalPanel(
      condition = "input.show_quantile_quantile",
      class = "side-panel",
      shiny::tags$h4("QQ-Plot (Most Recent Sample)"),
      shiny::plotOutput(outputId = "most_recent_sample", height = "250px")
    )
  )
)

widget_server <- function(input, output, session) {
  shiny::observeEvent(eventExpr = input$dataset, ignoreInit = TRUE, handlerExpr = {
    shiny::req(input$dataset %in% dataset_names)
    attribute_choices <- attribute_choices_by_dataset[[input$dataset]]
    shiny::updateSelectInput(session = session, inputId = "attribute", choices = attribute_choices, selected = attribute_choices[[1L]])
  })

  # The formula is read once typing pauses, so half-typed formulas are not evaluated.
  formula_text <- shiny::debounce(r = shiny::reactive(x = input$transform_formula), millis = 600)

  # The selected attribute's population, transformed by the formula while Apply Transform is checked.
  # A formula that cannot produce a valid population replaces both plots with a message saying why.
  population <- shiny::reactive(x = {
    shiny::req(input$attribute %in% names(x = population_catalog))
    attribute_population <- population_catalog[[input$attribute]]
    if (!isTRUE(x = input$apply_transform)) {
      return(attribute_population)
    }
    outcome <- tryCatch(
      expr = transform_population(population = attribute_population, formula_text = formula_text()),
      formula_problem = function(condition) condition
    )
    if (inherits(x = outcome, what = "formula_problem")) {
      shiny::validate(conditionMessage(c = outcome))
    }
    outcome
  })

  simulation <- shiny::reactive(x = {
    shiny::req(input$sample_size, input$number_of_samples)
    simulate_sample_means(
      population = population(),
      sample_size = as.integer(x = input$sample_size),
      number_of_samples = as.integer(x = input$number_of_samples)
    )
  })

  # Both plots size their labels and margins to the drawing area, so they are redrawn, not rescaled,
  # when the main plot widens or narrows as the quantile-quantile checkbox is toggled.
  output$sampling_distribution <- shiny::renderPlot(
    expr = draw_sampling_distribution(simulation = simulation()),
    res = 96,
    execOnResize = TRUE,
    bg = "transparent"
  )
  output$most_recent_sample <- shiny::renderPlot(
    expr = draw_most_recent_sample(simulation = simulation()),
    res = 96,
    execOnResize = TRUE,
    bg = "transparent"
  )
}
```

## {#widget}

```{css}
/* The widget fills the whole content area of its untitled slide. */
slides > slide > hgroup + article#widget {
  margin-top: 0;
  height: 100%;
}
article#widget > iframe.shiny-frame {
  height: 100%;
  border: 0;
  background: transparent;
}
```

```{r widget}
shiny::shinyApp(ui = widget_interface, server = widget_server, options = list(width = "100%", height = 620))
```
